title: Marcelo Caetano succeeds Salazar
summary: Salazar was incapacitated in early August 1968 by a haemorrhage after a fall, and on 27 September President Américo Tomás appointed Marcelo Caetano President of the Council in his place. Caetano offered "evolution in continuity": some liberalisation of censorship and of the political police, a wider electoral roll, and reformist deputies allowed into the National Assembly, but no negotiated end to the colonial war and no opening to opposition parties. Salazar recovered enough to believe himself still in office and was never told otherwise; he died in July 1970. The limits of the opening were clear by 1970, and the officers who made the 1974 coup came out of the war Caetano had not ended. It is in the atlas as the hinge between the regime built by one man and the six years in which his successor tried to reform it without touching what made reform necessary.
